title: The parameters that matter: presolve, cuts, heuristics, focus

questions.stem: A service passes MathOpt's SolveParameters(heuristics=Emphasis.VERY_HIGH) to HiGHS. No error is raised, and the LP iterations of every run match the default's exactly. What explains it?

options.text: HiGHS already runs its heuristics at the highest effort by default
options.says: HiGHS's default heuristic effort is 0.05 on a scale to 1, and raising its own option to 0.8 changed the run.

options.text: HiGHS takes the common knob but does not act on it; its own option works
options.says: Right: the common knob was accepted at every level with no effect, while mip_heuristic_effort changed the LP iterations.

options.text: HiGHS refused the common knob, and the service swallowed the error
options.says: HiGHS took the heuristics knob; the one it refused was cuts.

options.text: HiGHS's heuristics had nothing left to find, so no setting moves its work
options.says: Its own option did move the work: mip_heuristic_effort 0.8 took the Valley plan from 29,414 to 31,900 LP iterations.

origin.section: Four Knobs, and Each Solver Names Them Differently

questions.stem: A dispatch service needs a plan within 1% of optimal as early as possible and stops as soon as it has one; it never needs the proof. Going by the lesson's SCIP tables, which setting suits it best?

options.text: Heuristics OFF, since plans from the tree alone come sooner
options.says: With heuristics off, SCIP needed 10.74 times the work to a plan within 1%, and lost all 24 pairs.

options.text: Emphasis OPTIMALITY, since it closes the whole gap sooner
options.says: OPTIMALITY was slower on both measures: 1.41 to a good plan and 1.14 to proof.

options.text: Presolve OFF, since skipping presolve brought good plans sooner
options.says: On SCIP, presolve off brought good plans later, not sooner: 1.38 of the default's work to a plan within 1%, 9 wins and 15 losses.

options.text: Emphasis FEASIBILITY, since good plans came with less work
options.says: Right: 0.39 of the default's work to a plan within 1%, 20 wins and 1 loss; its slower proof does not matter here.

origin.section: Focus Says Which Side of the Gap to Work On

questions.stem: A colleague changes Gurobi's Presolve, Cuts and MIPFocus in one commit, and the work to proof drops 20% over the team's instance set and seeds. What does that result show?

options.text: That the three together cut the work, not which of them did it
options.says: Right: knobs changed together cannot tell you which one did the work; change one at a time.

options.text: That each of the three helped, since together they cut the work
options.says: A joint result says nothing about each knob; one may have helped and another hurt.

options.text: That Presolve did most of the work, the other two little or none
options.says: Knobs changed together cannot tell you which one did the work; Presolve may have helped, hurt or done nothing.

options.text: That MIPFocus did most of the work, the other two little or none
options.says: Knobs changed together cannot tell you which one did the work; MIPFocus may have helped, hurt or done nothing.

origin.section: Defaults Win Here, So Change One Knob at a Time and Keep the Default Unless Both Measures Agree
